subject: Final signoff: L4 SWE package — tradeoffs between base and equity
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: L4 SWE (Alex Romero) — final package recommendation and quick tradeoffs

Team —

I ran through Marissa's comp worksheet (attached) and sketched a final recommended package for Alex Romero (SWE L4, relocating from SF). Need quick signoff so Recruiting can send the offer today. High-level recommendation below, followed by the tradeoffs and why I'm leaning this way.

Recommended package (total target):
- Base: $165,000
- Variable (annual bonus target): 10% (performance-based)
- Equity: 18-month RSU grant, cliff at 12 months, $55k value at grant in 4-year vest schedule pro-rated to 18 months (structured as 0.9 years equivalent of standard 4-year RSUs)
- Sign-on: $20,000 (relocation / retention)
- Start date: target 2025-11-03

Rationale / tradeoffs:
- Budget headroom: this sits near the 60th percentile for L4 for the SF comp band in our worksheet. It keeps base slightly below midpoint but compensates with a stronger immediate RSU and sign-on to address relocation expectations.
- Candidate preference: Alex signaled preference for stability but indicated equity is important given their current startup upside. A heavier RSU component reduces run-rate cash spend but is attractive to candidate.
- Hiring manager alignment: Vikram (hiring manager) asked for market-competitive cash for relocation but is okay with a slightly higher equity mix.

Requesting:
1) Karthik — confirm headcount/finance ok with this mix (comp will sit on Eng SRE cost center 2204).
2) Marissa — confirm midpoint percentile calculations and whether RSU math needs to shift if we convert more to base.
3) Lauren — confirm approval authority required or whether I can sign off as hiring manager for this package.

Attachments: comp_worksheet_Q3_2025.xlsx (rows highlighted), draft offer PDF (offer_L4_SWE_standard.pdf) is a stub, Recruiting will populate candidate details after signoff.

Thanks —
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Eng Manager, Compute
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: L4 SWE (Alex Romero) — final package recommendation and quick tradeoffs

Grace —

Quick read: finance is OK with the total comp target and cost center 2204 (we have ~3.2% headroom this quarter). Two comments:

- If we push more into RSU (as proposed), monthly cash-burn decreases which looks good for run-rate. However, since sign-on is $20k, total first-year cash impact is still ~ $185k (base + sign-on). Confirm that Recruiting is prepared to fund relocation upfront and expense it to EMEA relocation ledger? I think that's fine but want it noted.

- Approvals: this package crosses $170k cash threshold for discretionary manager signoff? Our delegation table says anything >$170k base requires BizOps approval. Since base is $165k, we're technically under that, but combined cash (base + sign) triggers a heads-up to BizOps in the offer email. I can loop BizOps if you prefer.

Approve headcount and comp mix from Finance side. I defer to Marissa on exact percentile calls.

Karthik
Director, Finance Partnering

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: L4 SWE (Alex Romero) — final package recommendation and quick tradeoffs

Grace/Karthik —

I reviewed the Q3 comp worksheet and updated a few cells (see attachment). Short summary:
- $165k base = ~58th percentile vs our internal L4 SF band median ($158k median, $175k 75th).
- $55k equity value at grant (~market-value using our fair market multiplier) puts total 1st-year on-target comp around $250k when you include sign-on + pro-rated equity.
- If we wanted to move to a higher base (move to $175k), to stay within the same total target we'd need to reduce RSU value by ~ $20k (to maintain budget target). That increases immediate cash obligations and would push us over the $170k base discretionary boundary Karthik flagged (requiring BizOps signoff).

My recommendation: keep the proposed mix (165k base + $55k equity + $20k sign-on). It maximizes candidate preference for equity while minimizing the signoff friction. Also keeps our comp philosophy consistent for L4 standard offers.

Attachment notes: comp_worksheet_Q3_2025.xlsx — tab "L4_SF_AlexR" has the percentile chart and alternate scenarios (base+no sign-on, base+larger sign-on, higher-base lower-rsu).

Approved from Total Rewards perspective.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Total Rewards Partner
